newsitem.title: USA: Two explosions hit Atlanta abortion clinic.
newsitem.headline: Two explosions hit Atlanta abortion clinic.

text.p: Two bombs exploded about an hour apart outside an Atlanta abortion clinic on Thursday, the second one injuring six people including federal agents who were called in to investigate the initial blast.

Fears of a third bomb kept explosives experts combing through the area for hours, protected by special armoured suits and assisted by bomb-sniffing dogs. The search was expected to continue long after dark.

The first blast shattered the southwest side of an office building housing the Atlanta Northside Family Planning Services centre in a suburb known as Sandy Springs at around 9:30 a.m. EST (1430 GMT). Officials said at least one clinic worker was inside at the time but no one was injured.

About an hour later, a garbage container in the corner of an adjacent parking lot exploded, knocking people to the ground and injuring several at the scene including agents from the FBI and the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF). Six people were sent to local hospitals for treatment.

Although federal officials said the clinic appeared to be the target of the attack, U.S. Attorney Kent Alexander said he could not rule out the possibility that the bombing was an unrelated act of domestic terrorism, perhaps one directed at law enforcement.

"Every resource available is going to be put on this. Teams of ATF experts, teams of FBI experts are en route now. We've got a lot of local experts as well. This is a bombing we intend to solve," he told a news conference held about a quarter mile from the building.
Investigators were checking for any links to last summer's Centennial Olympic Park bombing, which left two people dead and more than 100 injured in July. No one has been charged in that incident.
"As far as any connection with the Centennial Park bombing ... we will know fairly quickly whether there's a similarity or not," said Alexander.

Investigators would not discuss the makeup of Thursday's bombs. But a state investigator reported finding nails in an office building located dozens of yards (metres) away. Plate-glass windows in the same building were shattered by the initial blast.

Police tightened security for at least half a dozen abortion clinics in the metropolitan area. "I've made certain that the police reinforcements are very visible as a way of reassuring the public," Atlanta Mayor Bill Campbell said.
But that did not stop bomb threats to two other Atlanta facilities.
Anti-abortion activists attacked three abortion clinics in the Atlanta area in 1984, including the same facility involved in Thursday's bombing. No one was ever prosecuted for those attacks.
In Washington, President Bill Clinton condemned the violence, calling it "a vile and malevolent act."

"Nobody has a right to use violence in America to advance their own convictions over the rights of others," Clinton said in a statement. "We will get to the bottom of this. We will punish those responsible to the fullest extent that the law provides."
